reading: A snowbound country-house murder told from below stairs, in which the housekeeper's timeline, a tallow stub and a candle box are set against the Major's parade-ground version of the night. Three lines branch from the same first act: one names the Major by a servant's word and breaks the household doing it; one names the innocent fiancée and lets the killer carve at dinner; one lets the key in the lock speak and gets the housekeeper the next cart. It reads as a tightly built fair-play puzzle whose physical clues (stub, box, keyhole, glass, scrap) carry the plot, with the real tension in what each solution costs the people who hand you the evidence.

best_thing: T3N04 The Keyhole Filled: the housekeeper pulls the master's key from the Major's waistcoat and sets it in the lock from the gallery so the kneeling solicitor, widow and doctor see the keyhole go dark. It turns the N01 glimpse of the lamp into a demonstration anyone can watch, convicts without a servant's word, and still costs her the house.
worst_thing: T2's branch point: the line text says it leaves after N03 when you caught the widow on her knees at the keyhole with her hairpin and traded silence for silence, but no node shows that scene; N03 contains only the rounds and the valet. The whole wrong-passenger line hangs on an event the player never plays.
